questions.text: Write a function to return the sum of two numbers. The input will be two space-separated integers on a single line.
Write a program to reverse a given string. The input will be a single line containing a string.
What is a Star topology? Describe its main advantage and main disadvantage.
questions.expected_answer: A star topology is a network structure where all individual nodes or devices are connected directly to a central device, such as a hub or a switch. Main advantage: Easy to add or remove devices without disrupting the network, and the failure of one node or cable does not affect other nodes. Main disadvantage: High dependency on the central device; if the central hub or switch fails, the entire network becomes unavailable.
questions.rubric: 1 mark for defining Star topology and mentioning the central device. 1 mark for correctly stating a valid advantage. 1 mark for correctly stating a valid disadvantage.

questions.text: Explain the structure of a Bus topology and describe how data travels along the network.
questions.expected_answer: In a bus topology, all network devices are connected to a single central cable called the backbone or bus. Data is transmitted along the bus as electronic signals. As data travels, each connected device checks the destination address; if the address matches the device, it processes the data, otherwise it ignores it. Terminators at both ends of the cable absorb signals to prevent reflection.
questions.rubric: 1 mark for describing the central backbone cable structure. 1 mark for explaining how data travels and is filtered by destination addresses/terminated.

questions.text: Compare Mesh topology and Ring topology with respect to redundancy and cabling requirements.
questions.expected_answer: Redundancy: Mesh topology offers very high redundancy because devices have multiple dedicated links, allowing alternate paths if a link fails. Ring topology has low redundancy because data travels sequentially, so a single break can disable the loop (unless a dual ring is used). Cabling Requirements: Mesh topology requires a very large amount of cabling due to point-to-point connections between nodes. Ring topology requires much less cabling, as each node only connects to its two immediate neighbors.
questions.rubric: 1.5 marks for accurately comparing redundancy between Mesh and Ring. 1.5 marks for accurately comparing cabling requirements between Mesh and Ring.

questions.text: What is a Hybrid topology? Provide one practical example of how it is implemented.
questions.expected_answer: A hybrid topology is a network architecture created by combining two or more different standard network topologies (such as Star, Bus, or Ring) into a single network. A common practical example is a Star-Bus topology, where individual departments in a building use star networks connected to a central bus backbone line.
questions.rubric: 1 mark for defining Hybrid topology as a combination of two or more distinct topologies. 1 mark for giving a valid, accurate practical example.

questions.text: Why is a Mesh topology considered highly fault-tolerant, and what is its primary drawback?
questions.expected_answer: Mesh topology is highly fault-tolerant because every node is connected via redundant point-to-point links to other nodes. If one link fails, network traffic can be seamlessly rerouted through alternative paths without causing downtime. Its primary drawback is the high cost and extreme complexity associated with installing and managing the extensive amount of cabling and I/O ports.
questions.rubric: 1 mark for explaining why it is fault-tolerant (redundant paths/rerouting). 1 mark for stating the primary drawback (high cost/cabling complexity).
